newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI details implementation to date of RTGS system.
newsitem.headline: EMI details implementation to date of RTGS system.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute (EMI) on Friday gave details of how far European countries had got in adopting real time gross settlement (RTGS) systems.
RTGS is a real-time settlement system in which processing and settlement take place on an order-by-order basis.

In a report on the operating framework of the future European Central Bank, the EMI said Denmark, Germany, Sweden and Finland have had the systems in operation since 1995 and the United Kingdom, Belgium and Portugal implemented RTGS in 1996.

"In all other countries, RTGS systems will be implemented or the existing systems will incorporate significant technical modifications to meet TARGET's (Trans-European Automated Real-Time Gross settlement Express Transfer) specifications in the course of 1997," it added.
A functioning RTGS system is needed for participation in TARGET, the system intended to allow smooth payments transfers in euros.
